# Media Puppies

> Paid media team for agencies and businesses in the United States, United Kingdom, Canada and Australia.
> We run Google Ads and Meta (Facebook and Instagram) ads as a white label partner for marketing agencies,
> and as a dedicated media buyer for brands. The team is based in Noida, India, so account work and
> reporting happen while US and UK clients sleep. Month to month, no lock-in, never a percentage of ad spend.

Updated 2026-11-19. 272 articles, 29 free calculators, 73 service and market pages.

## Key facts

- Services: white label PPC and paid social for agencies; dedicated media buyer; Google Ads; Meta ads; LinkedIn ads; SEO; AI automation.
- Markets served: United States, United Kingdom, Canada, Australia, United Arab Emirates and India.
- Team location: Noida, Delhi NCR, India. Invoiced to clients in their own currency.
- Pricing model: a fixed monthly fee per account, month to month. Never a percentage of ad spend. The fee depends on the account and is given on the first call, after an audit.
- White label terms: mutual NDA and non-solicit before access; the end client's ad accounts stay in the client's name; reporting in the agency's own template.
- First step for a new account: a written audit within two working days of access.
- Contact: info@mediapuppies.com

## Original research (our own data, free to cite with a link)

Hub: https://mediapuppies.com/research/

- [Google Ads management fees: what 29 US, UK and Australian agencies publish](https://mediapuppies.com/blog/google-ads-management-fees-study/): Of 29 agencies that publish their own Google Ads management fees, 18 (62.07%) charge only a fixed monthly fee. 8 publish a percentage of ad spend anywhere on their pages. The median lowest published monthly fee was US$775 in the US (10 agencies, US$199 to US$6,000), £499.50 in the UK (8, £179 to £2,000) and A$600 in Australia (5, A$330 to A$1,995). Published percentages ran from 12% to 15% of spend in the US, 6% to 11% in the UK and 12% to 20% in Australia. 5 agencies use a "greater of" fee or percentage. Only 6 of 29 state a minimum ad spend and 6 print a setup fee amount. 15 say nothing about setup. 8 of the 19 agencies that state a contract length say rolling or no lock-in, and 10 of the 13 that state notice ask for 30 days. 4 show a longer minimum term on another page or in their terms.
- [HVAC Google Ads cost by country: click prices in the US, Canada, Australia and the UK](https://mediapuppies.com/blog/hvac-google-ads-cost/): On Ahrefs estimates of 17 November 2026, the median HVAC buyer search cost $2.50 a click in the US, $2 in Canada, $1.80 in Australia and $0.70 in the UK. 100 clicks at the median: $250, $200, $180 and $70. US emergency HVAC searches had a median of $19 a click against $2 for the other 29 US buyer searches, a premium of 9.5x. "Emergency hvac service" was the dearest at $30. In the UK the 3 emergency searches cost $0.15, and Australia had none in its top 50. The US top 50 HVAC list carried 30.42 times the monthly searches of the UK list and 68 times the Australian one. Half of the Australian list was not homeowner demand, and its dearest rows were HVAC software at $45 a click. Canadian city searches were the dearest HVAC clicks outside the US: a median of $6 across 7 keywords, led by "hvac kingston" at $8. On 7 US HVAC keywords in both tools, Ahrefs priced clicks at a median 11.31% of Semrush. Semrush put "hvac repair" at $30.91 and Ahrefs at $0.30.
- [Marketing agency terms and conditions: what 20 agency contracts say about notice, minimum term and who owns the ad account](https://mediapuppies.com/blog/marketing-agency-terms-and-conditions/): Of 37 agency terms pages we collected, 17 (45.9%) only cover use of the website. 20 hold real contract clauses: 3 from the US, 9 from the UK and 8 from Australia. 15 of the 20 contracts state a client notice period. The median is 30 days and the range is 0 to 60. 9 of 20 (45%) let the client leave at any time on notice, and 9 of 20 have some lock-in: a minimum term, an exit only at the end of a term, or an early-exit charge. Only 3 of 20 terms pages (15%) say who owns the ad account. 2 say the client and 1 says new accounts the agency sets up stay the agency's. 17 (85%) are silent, although 6 of the 20 agencies promise client ownership on a sales page. 7 of 20 (35%) let fees change during the contract, and 3 (15%) build in a yearly rise of 5% or CPI. 18 of 20 (90%) cap the agency's liability, most often at 3 months of fees. On 6 of 20 agencies (30%), the pricing or services page says something different from the terms page. In 3, "no lock-in" or "30-day rolling" sits beside a 3 or 6 month minimum or a cancellation fee.
- [Plumber Google Ads cost in 2026: click prices in the US, UK, Canada and Australia](https://mediapuppies.com/blog/plumber-google-ads-cost/): On Ahrefs estimates of 17 November 2026, the median plumber buyer search cost $8 a click in Australia, $7 in the US, $7 in Canada and $4 in the UK. 100 clicks at the median: $800, $700, $700 and $400. US plumber clicks are priced on urgency. Emergency, 24 hour and same day searches had a median of $12.50, 4.17 times the $3 median of other US plumber searches. In Canada urgent searches came in below the rest, at 0.64 times. Canada prices the city name. "plumber" and "plumber near me" were $2.50 each, while the 26 Canadian city searches had a median of $8, and all 26 cost more than "plumber". The UK had the cheapest head term in our data, $1.90 for "plumber", and two of the dearest UK clicks: "emergency plumber london" and "emergency plumber croydon" at $20 each. On 4 US plumber keywords in both tools, Ahrefs priced clicks at a median 39.14% of Semrush. Semrush put "emergency plumber" at $43.65 and Ahrefs at $20.
- [PPC agency CPC in 2026: what agencies pay per click for their own clients in the US, UK, Canada and Australia](https://mediapuppies.com/blog/ppc-agency-keywords-cpc/): On Ahrefs estimates of 17 November 2026, the median buyer search containing "ppc agency" cost $12 a click in the UK, $7.50 in Australia, $5 in Canada and $3.50 in the US. 100 clicks at the median: $1,200, $750, $500 and $350. The UK agency median was the highest of all 36 country and trade medians in our wider CPC study, and 2.0 times the UK locksmith median. The US splits in two. Searches that name a niche, a business model, white label or a city had a median of $7 (23 keywords); generic wordings such as "ppc marketing agency" had a median of $0.35 (18 keywords), 20.0 times cheaper. The single word pair "ppc agency" cost $20 in the US and $25 in the UK. In the US that is 6.67 times the median of the other 41 priced agency searches. Most agency searches in Australia and Canada are too rare for Ahrefs to price: 68% of the Australian top 50 and 66% of the Canadian top 50 had no CPC, against 10% in the US.
- [Roofing Google Ads cost in 2026: what a roofer click costs in the US, UK, Canada and Australia](https://mediapuppies.com/blog/roofer-google-ads-cost/): On Ahrefs estimates of 17 November 2026, the median roofer buyer search cost $4.00 a click in Australia, $3.50 in the UK, $3.50 in Canada and $1.45 in the US. 100 clicks at those medians: $400, $350, $350 and $145. The US figure is thin. Only 8 of 41 US buyer keywords for "roofer" had any price, and 32 of the unpriced rows were neighbourhood or business-park names. In the UK, 43 of 46 had a price. Semrush prices US roofing job searches far higher: a median of $20.27 across 25 keywords such as "roof repair" and "roofing company", 13.98 times the Ahrefs US roofer median. Semrush had "roofers near me" at $26.83, while Ahrefs had "roofer near me" at $1.50. "Emergency roofer" was the dearest roofer keyword in any country, $20 in the US, or 14.29 times the word "roofer". In the UK emergency searches cost 0.88 times "roofer", and Australia had none in its top 50. Outside the US, roofer clicks sat a little above each country's home-services median, at 114.29% to 116.67% of it. In the US they sat at 44.62%.
- [What PPC management includes: we compared the service pages of 37 agencies](https://mediapuppies.com/blog/what-ppc-management-includes/): The median agency named 15 of our 33 PPC tasks on its public pages, with a range of 2 to 29. Only reporting was listed by more than three in four agencies (84%). Basic account hygiene was rarely spelled out. 41% listed negative keyword work and 62% conversion tracking. Only 10 of 37 (27%) named negatives, conversion tracking and ad testing together. On reporting cadence, 15 agencies promised a monthly report, 4 a weekly one and 6 only a live dashboard. 12 (32%) gave no cadence at all. 46% promised a dedicated account manager and 41% regular calls or meetings. 13 agencies (35%) mentioned neither. US pages were the most explicit: 69% named an account manager, against 38% in the UK and 27% in Australia. Microsoft Ads was listed by 65% of agencies (85% in the UK), Google Shopping or Performance Max by 68%, and Local Services Ads by 16%. Agencies that publish their fees listed more: a median of 18 tasks against 13, and Microsoft Ads 83% against 36%. Part of that gap is because we also read their pricing pages.
- [White label PPC providers compared: what 25 providers offer, and what their pages leave out](https://mediapuppies.com/blog/white-label-ppc-providers-compared/): Of 25 white label PPC providers we read on 19 November 2026, 21 (84%) named Google Ads in their offer, 11 (44%) Meta, 10 (40%) Microsoft Advertising and 1 (4%) Amazon. 8 (32%) named Google Ads and nothing else. Branded reporting is the standard promise: 18 (72%) said reports carry the agency brand. 9 (36%) said the end client never sees the provider, and 3 (12%) said they will talk to the client under the agency brand if asked. Prices are mostly private. 5 providers (20%) published amounts and 12 (48%) said nothing about their own pricing. 2 said outright that they do not take a cut of ad spend. The terms that protect an agency were the rarest lines on the pages: 7 (28%) said month to month or no contract, 4 (16%) mentioned an NDA and 4 (16%) said who owns or accesses the ad account. The median page answered 5 of 11 checks an agency would want settled before signing, and the best answered 8. NDA mentions came from 3 of 6 India-based providers and 1 of 19 elsewhere.
- [Google Ads for electricians: what a click costs in the US, UK, Canada and Australia](https://mediapuppies.com/blog/electrician-google-ads-cost/): On Ahrefs estimates collected on 17 November 2026, the median buyer electrician keyword cost $6.00 a click in Australia, $4.00 in the US, $2.50 in Canada and $2.25 in the UK. Australia was the only market above the US, at 150% of the US median. City searches drove it: 14 Australian city keywords had a median of $7.00, and the US top 50 held no city keywords at all. Emergency searches cost the most in three of four countries. In the US the emergency median was $7.00 against $3.25 for other electrician searches, 2.15 times as much. Australia was 1.42 times and the UK 1.32 times. On the 5 US keywords both tools priced, Ahrefs was a median 30.77% of Semrush. "Emergency electrician" was $21.57 in Semrush and $0.15 in Ahrefs. The dearest clicks around the trade are sold to electricians: "electrician liability insurance" was $30 in the UK, and the top buyer keyword in any country was $10.
- [Law firm PPC by country: what lawyer clicks cost on Google Ads in the US, UK, Canada and Australia](https://mediapuppies.com/blog/lawyer-google-ads-cost-by-country/): On Ahrefs estimates of 17 November 2026, the median buyer-intent lawyer CPC was $4.50 in Australia, $2.75 in the US, $2.75 in Canada and $2.50 in the UK. Australia's median was 163.64% of the US figure. The US had the longest tail: 11 of its 40 priced buyer keywords (27.5%) cost $10 or more, topped by "motorcycle accident lawyer" at $70. In the UK it was 3 of 31 (9.68%). On the 20 US legal keywords both tools priced, Ahrefs was lower than Semrush on all 20. The medians were $3.50 against $40.90, and on 6 of the 11 injury keywords Ahrefs came in under 1% of the Semrush price. On the 10 lawyer keywords found in all four countries, the median UK price was 119.84% of the US price, Australia 175.71% and Canada 85.71%. The US was the dearest market on only 1 of the 10. Injury and compensation searches had a median of $8 in Australia against $4 for other practice areas, 2.0 times as much. In the US, Ahrefs priced 12 of 24 injury keywords under $1.50, which pulled that median down to $1.85.
- [Locksmith Google Ads cost in 2026: what a click costs in the US, UK, Canada and Australia](https://mediapuppies.com/blog/locksmith-google-ads-cost/): On Ahrefs estimates of 17 November 2026, the median locksmith buyer search cost $6 a click in the UK, $3 in the US, $3 in Canada and $2.25 in Australia. 100 clicks at the median: $600, $300, $300 and $225. On the 11 locksmith keywords priced in all four countries, the UK was dearer than the US on 8. Australia and Canada were never dearer than the US on any of them, with medians at 72% of the US price. City searches cost more than the plain word "locksmith". The US city median was $5 against $3 for "locksmith", and 15 of 18 US city searches were priced above it. The dearest single terms were "locksmith st kilda" at $16 and "locksmith croydon" at $12. Emergency locksmith searches carried a small premium or none: 1.17x other locksmith searches in the US, 1.32x in Australia, 0.83x in the UK and 0.53x in Canada (2 keywords only). On 6 US locksmith keywords in both tools, Ahrefs priced clicks at a median 52.48% of Semrush. Semrush put "emergency locksmith" at $6.62 and Ahrefs at $3.50.
- [Pest control Google Ads cost in 2026: what a click costs in the US, UK, Australia and Canada](https://mediapuppies.com/blog/pest-control-google-ads-cost/): On Ahrefs estimates collected 17 November 2026, the median buyer-intent pest control click cost $6 in the US, $3.50 in Australia, $3 in Canada and $2 in the UK. The UK median was 33.33% of the US one. Commercial searches were the dearest US pest control clicks: "commercial pest control near me" at $18 and "commercial pest control" at $13. Their median was 2.58 times the other US buyer searches. 20 of the 50 highest-volume US pest control searches were brand names of other firms, with a median CPC of $2.50. Outside the US, city searches filled the lists: their median was $4.50 in Australia, $3.50 in Canada and $2.50 in the UK. On the 7 buyer keywords found in all four countries, the median UK price was 25% of the US price, Canada 28.57% and Australia 50%. Semrush prices US pest control higher: a median of $14.84 across 17 keywords on 3 November 2026, with emergency and same-day searches at $24.41, 1.98 times the rest. On the 3 keywords both tools priced, Ahrefs was 48.67% of Semrush.
- [B2B PPC cost per click: what software, insurance and finance keywords cost (2026)](https://mediapuppies.com/blog/b2b-ppc-cost-per-click/): The median Semrush CPC estimate for 10 US software keywords was $28.87, against $12.32 for all 339 keywords we priced, and 60% of the software keywords were at $20 or more. Payroll software was the most expensive software keyword at $50.14 a click; erp software was the cheapest at $11.96. Insurance had the highest median of 11 industries at $35.44; its 4 quote searches had a median of $71.04, and business insurance was $39.38. Finance had a median of $9.47, sixth of 11 industries and below the $12.32 overall median, while small business loans was $20.57. On 3 November 2026, Google showed an AI Overview on all 10 software searches in the US, and on all 10 in the UK, Canada and Australia too.
- [PPC for dentists: implant clicks cost up to 2.33 times a dentist click, and what 353 implant ads offer](https://mediapuppies.com/blog/dental-implant-ppc/): On Semrush's US estimates of 3 November 2026, "dental implants near me" cost $17.88 a click, 2.15 times "dentist near me" ($8.30). "Same day dental implants" cost $19.34, 2.33 times. Implant and denture searches had a median of $10.26 a click, 1.5 times general and emergency dental searches. Price research is cheaper: "dental implants cost" was $6.14. Of 353 live US implant ads in the Meta Ad Library on 17 November 2026, 22.4% stated a price. Across 15 US practices that named a per-arch price, the median lowest price was $13,995. One advertiser ran 75 of the 353 ads (21.2%), while 71.0% of the 169 advertisers ran a single ad. 59 advertisers (34.9%) shared blocks of ad copy with at least two other practices, and 42 sent clicks to subdomains of one shared landing-page domain.
- [Google Ads audit by search intent: which searches to cut, from 339 US keyword prices and their AI Overviews](https://mediapuppies.com/blog/google-ads-audit-search-intent/): Cost research was the cheapest of six home services intent groups we priced: a median Semrush US CPC estimate of $6.21, against $27.91 for emergency searches, 4.49 times as much. 91.7% of 36 US cost questions showed an AI Overview, and all 33 of those AI Overviews quoted a dollar figure. None of the 33 showed a business rating, phone number or address. Near me searches showed an AI Overview only 34.4% of the time, and 14 of the 21 that did named a business with a rating, phone or address. Adding near me moved home services prices very little: it cost more in 9 of 17 keyword pairs, with a median difference of $0.21. In dental it cost more in 7 of 9 pairs. In law, personal injury keywords had a median estimated CPC of $156, 16.08 times the $9.70 median of 22 other practice keywords.
- [Google Ads CPC by country: US vs UK vs Canada vs Australia, and why Ahrefs and Semrush disagree on price](https://mediapuppies.com/blog/google-ads-cpc-by-country/): On the 52 US keywords both tools priced, Ahrefs' CPC was lower than Semrush's on every one. The median Ahrefs figure was 36.52% of the Semrush figure, and 13 keywords (25%) came in under a tenth. The tools did not even agree on order: the rank correlation was 0.16, and only 4 of Semrush's 10 most expensive keywords were in Ahrefs' top 10. "Personal injury lawyer near me" was $128.80 in Semrush and $0.20 in Ahrefs. Within Ahrefs, on 71 identical keywords found in all four countries, the median UK CPC was 53.33% of the US price, Canada 62.5% and Australia 80%. Emergency home-service searches cost 3.33 times other home-service searches in the US, 2.67 times in Australia, 1.8 times in the UK and 1.0 times in Canada. By trade, Australia had the highest median CPC for plumber, electrician, roofer and lawyer searches; the UK for locksmith and PPC agency searches; the US for HVAC, pest control and dental implants.
- [HVAC Local Services Ads vs Google Ads: what a lead and a click cost in 2026, and what 196 HVAC ads on Facebook offer](https://mediapuppies.com/blog/hvac-lsa-vs-google-ads/): On Semrush's US estimates of 3 November 2026, the median HVAC keyword cost $19.60 a click. Emergency searches had a median of $35.71 and repair searches $27.85, 1.95 times the $14.30 median for install and replacement searches. The head of one agency said HVAC Local Services Ads leads rose from $51 to $60 in a year, up 17.6%. A second agency put peak-season phone leads at $45 to $55, rising to $70 to $80 in slow months. At the median click price, a $60 LSA lead costs the same as 3.06 clicks. Search ads only match it if 32.7% of clicks become leads. For emergency clicks the bar is 59.5%. Of 477 active US ads that the Meta Ad Library returned for HVAC searches on 17 November 2026, 196 came from 165 local HVAC contractors. 87.9% of those contractors ran one ad, and 63.3% of the ads sent people to a website. 26.5% of the contractor ads pushed a tune-up or maintenance visit, and 7 advertisers named a price from $59 to $150. Only 16.3% used 24/7 or emergency wording, though emergency clicks are the dearest HVAC clicks on Google.
- [Plumber leads in 2026: what a Google Ads click, a Local Services Ads lead and an Angi lead cost](https://mediapuppies.com/blog/plumber-leads-google-ads-vs-lsa-vs-angi/): On Semrush's US estimates of 3 November 2026, the median plumbing keyword cost $23.29 a click, and emergency plumbing searches cost a median $40.98, 1.86 times the price of repair searches. In a video uploaded 28 October 2026, the head of one agency said his clients' plumbing Local Services Ads leads fell from $70 to $66 in a year, the only one of 5 trades he named that got cheaper. A software vendor's video puts a plumbing Angi lead at $40 to $85. Angi's CEO told investors pros pay $50 a lead and win one in 7 or 8, which is $350 to $400 of leads per job won. At the median click price, a $66 LSA lead costs the same as 2.83 clicks. On cost per lead, search ads only match it if 35.3% of clicks become a lead, and 62.1% if you buy emergency clicks. Of 28 plumbing searches we checked on 3 November, 15 showed a Google AI Overview. Two high-volume service searches, emergency plumber and plumber near me, did not.
- [White label PPC vs winning clients yourself: what agencies pay per click (2026 data)](https://mediapuppies.com/blog/white-label-ppc-economics/): In Semrush US estimates from 3 November 2026, "google ads management" was $228.10 a click, the second highest of the 339 keywords we priced, and "ppc management" was $95.27. "white label ppc" was estimated at $14.28 a click, 164th of 339. The "google ads management" estimate is 16.0 times higher. Marketing services ranked 3rd of 11 industries by median estimated CPC ($22.49), behind insurance ($35.44) and software ($28.87). 14 of the 15 marketing services searches we checked in the US (93.3%) showed a Google AI Overview, against 57.8% across all 339 searches. Of the first 150 live US Facebook ads in the Ad Library containing "marketing agency", 34 (22.7%) were selling to agency owners, and 31 of the 52 agencies in the list (59.6%) had no offer, proof figure or risk reversal in the main text.
- [Facebook ads for home services: what 95 US firms, mostly plumbers and roofers, run, from five of our studies](https://mediapuppies.com/blog/facebook-ads-for-home-services/): Of 95 US home services firms with live Facebook or Instagram ads, 83.2% had only one ad in our sample, and the median ad had been live for 306 days. Home services used the widest spread of buttons: Learn more (18.8%), Contact us (17.1%), Get quote (14.5%) and Call now (14.5%). 23.1% of the ads had no link at all and asked people to call or message. 46.2% of the English ad texts made an offer, and 27.4% put it in the first line, the highest share of the five trades we studied. Only 57.7% of home services landing pages loaded the Meta pixel, the lowest of the five trades, and 28.8% weighed over 5 MB. 23.1% of 52 firms passed all four of our basics, and 82.8% of the 29 firms we looked up also ran Google ads in the last 30 days.
- [Real estate Facebook ads: what 87 US advertisers run, write and link to, from five of our studies](https://mediapuppies.com/blog/real-estate-facebook-ads/): Of 87 US real estate advertisers with live Facebook or Instagram ads, 92% had only one ad in our sample, and the median ad had been live for 347 days. Real estate ads were mostly single images (35.4%), dynamic creative (28.3%) and listing catalog ads (19.2%). Only 8.1% were videos, and 61.6% used a Learn more button. Only 34.5% of the English real estate ad texts made an offer, and 21.4% put it in the first line. 44.2% named a place, the highest of the five trades we studied. After the click, only 38.8% of real estate pages showed a phone link on the first screen of a phone, and 4.1% showed a form there. Only 14% of 43 real estate advertisers passed all four of our basics, the lowest of five trades, and 30.8% of the 26 we looked up ran Google ads in the last 30 days.
- [Facebook ads for dentists: what US dental practices run, write and link to, from five of our studies](https://mediapuppies.com/blog/facebook-ads-for-dentists/): Of 192 live US dental ads from 99 advertisers, one dental group ran 73 (38%), almost all of them videos. Without it, 42% of the other 119 ads were single images and 26.9% videos. Dental ads ran for a long time: the median ad had been live for 365 days, and 52.6% for over a year. 38.8% of English dental ad texts made an offer and 25% put it in the first line; of those with an offer, 77.8% put it in the first 150 characters, the highest share of the five trades. 71.5% used an exclamation mark, also the most of the five. Only 19.1% of 47 dental landing pages had a form, and 4.3% showed one on the first screen, while 72.3% showed a phone link there. 12 of the 47 pages came from one implant vendor; without them, 25.7% had a form. 29.8% of 47 dental advertisers passed all four of our basics, and 75% of the 28 dental advertisers we looked up also ran Google ads in the last 30 days.
- [Facebook ads for lawyers: what US law firms run, write and link to, from five of our studies](https://mediapuppies.com/blog/facebook-ads-for-lawyers/): Of 146 US law firms with live Facebook or Instagram ads, 69.9% had only one ad in our sample, and the median ad had been live for 181 days. Law firm ads used video (37%), dynamic creative (32.5%) and single images (24.9%). 38.9% used a Learn more button, and 18.9% had no link at all, asking people to call or message instead. 72.8% of law firm ad texts ran past 150 characters, the top of the 50 to 150 characters Meta suggests for single-image ads. Only 30.6% of the English texts made an offer such as a free consultation, and 12.8% put it in the first line. On the page after the click, 78.9% of law firms showed a phone link on the first screen of a phone, but only 7.9% showed a form there. Only 20.3% of 74 law firms passed all four of our basics, and 82.8% of the 29 firms we looked up also ran Google ads in the last 30 days.
- [Google Ads vs Facebook ads: we checked whether 142 US local businesses on Facebook also run Google ads](https://mediapuppies.com/blog/google-ads-vs-facebook-ads/): Of 142 US local businesses with live Facebook or Instagram ads, 64.1% had also shown Google ads in the US in the last 30 days, and 66.2% at any time. 33.8% showed no Google ads pointing to their website. Home service firms and law firms were the most likely to run both: 86.2% and 82.8% had shown Google ads at any time, and 75% of dentists. Med spas were at 50% and real estate businesses at 34.6%. Businesses whose landing page carried the Meta pixel were more likely to have run Google ads in the last 30 days (70.7%) than those where we saw no pixel (52%), though med spas went the other way. Of those with two or more Facebook ads in our sample, 78.3% had run Google ads in the last 30 days, against 61.3% of those with one. For 11 of the 94 businesses with Google ads, the first advertiser account shown was a marketing agency, a web design firm, a broadcaster or an ad platform.
- [Roof replacement ads: what 100 live US Facebook ads offer, and who runs them](https://mediapuppies.com/blog/roof-replacement-ads/): 73 of the first 100 live US ads for "roof replacement" came from roofing companies. 17 came from lead generation and roof cost sites, and 10 from products, franchises and other businesses. Among the 52 roofing companies, 42.3% gave some proof in the main text (reviews, years in business or a count of roofs), 40.4% offered a free inspection, estimate or quote, and 23.1% mentioned insurance or storm damage. Only 11.5% of the roofing companies mentioned financing in the main text, against 5 of the 13 lead and cost sites (38.5%). The lead sites also wrote a dollar figure more often (6 of 13, 46.2%, against 26.9%). 22 of the 52 roofing companies (42.3%) mentioned none of a free inspection, estimate or quote, financing, a warranty or a discount in the main text of any of their ads; 4 of those 22 did offer an instant online quote. One roofing company that quotes from satellite images ran 12 of the 100 ads, more than any other page.
- [Black Friday ads 2026: most of the top-listed ads in the Meta Ad Library started last year](https://mediapuppies.com/blog/black-friday-ads/): Of the 209 distinct ads among the first 100 live "black friday" ads listed for the US, UK, Canada and Australia, 56.5% started before 2026, most of them (105) during last year's Black Friday season. The median ad started 342 days before we read it. The default order probably favours long-running ads, so this describes the top of the list. The same online stores led all four countries. 38 ads were in the first 100 of every country, and only 14 of Canada's first 100 were in no other country's first 100. Only 56 of the 209 ads (26.8%) started this season, from 1 September 2026. Their median start was 29 October, 29 days before Black Friday, and 38 of them came from large retailers and well-known brands such as Walmart, Currys, Canadian Tire and Amazon Australia. 58.4% of the ads put a percentage in the main text, and among those the median top figure was 50%. 31.6% of all the ads wrote 50% or more, 37 of those 66 as "up to". 11 of this season's 56 ads (19.6%) used the word "early", against 13 of the 153 older ads (8.5%). Ten of the 11 came from large retailers and brands.
- [Marketing agency ads: we read 150 live US Facebook ads that mention "marketing agency"](https://mediapuppies.com/blog/marketing-agency-ads/): Only 54% of the first 150 live US ads mentioning "marketing agency" came from agencies selling to businesses. 22.7% sold to agency owners or would-be agency owners (12 of 93 pages; one page ran 14 of these ads), 13.3% were software or AI tools sold to businesses, and 10% were something else. The two pages with the most ads, 14 each, were an agency-building coach and a lead generation service for contractors. Half the 52 agencies (26) named the trade they serve, 22 trades in all, from fence and deck builders to churches. Another 6 named a region, and 20 were general. In the main ad text, 25% of the agencies included a dollar figure, a ROAS or multiple, or a count of leads or clients; 11.5% offered something free or an audit; and 11.5% offered a guarantee, pay for results or no contract. 31 of the 52 (59.6%) had none of the words or figures we searched for. 11 of the 15 software and AI tool pages mentioned AI or automation, and two of them opened by telling owners they could stop paying agency retainers.
- [Diwali ads 2026: who ran the top-listed Facebook and Instagram ads in the US, UK, Canada and Australia](https://mediapuppies.com/blog/diwali-ads/): Mainstream brands ran 59.4% of the 303 distinct live Diwali ads we read across the four countries. Indian and South Asian brands ran 26.1%, and 8.9% were ads aimed at people in India. Canada's list was the most mainstream: mainstream brands ran 81.9% of its top-listed Diwali ads (86 of 105), led by Walmart Canada with 13. In Australia they ran 25.3%. Of the 300 ads with a start date, the median began 14.5 days before Diwali, and 55.3% started between 15 and 31 October. Indian and South Asian brands used sale, offer or discount wording in 48.1% of their Diwali ads. Mainstream brands did so in 10%. 17.8% of mainstream brands' Diwali ads were partner posts, which the Library shows as a creator or publisher "with" the brand, such as Sheena Melwani with Lexus. Six mainstream pages from four companies used Hindi words written in English letters in their Diwali ads. Five of the six pages were Canadian, including Walmart Canada.
- [Facebook ad copy: what 1,098 live local-service ads shown in the US actually say](https://mediapuppies.com/blog/facebook-ad-copy/): In single-image ads, the format Meta's 50 to 150 character recommendation covers, the median primary text ran 256 characters and only 27.2% of 301 pieces of copy fell within the range. Across all formats the median was 298. Med spas wrote the longest copy (a 413-character median across formats) and used the most emojis: 65.8% of their copy had at least one, against 30.8% for law firms. 59.2% of the English copy told the reader what to do next, such as call, book or contact the business. Med spas did it most (72.1%) and real estate least (45.2%). 45% of the English copy mentioned an offer such as a free consultation, a price or a discount, and 60.8% of those put it within the first 150 characters. 19.8% of the copy opened with a question, and 22.3% of the English copy had an offer in its first line. Law firms opened with a question most often, in 26.3% of their copy. "You" outnumbered "we" in 51.6% of the English copy; "we" came out ahead in 19.7%.
- [Facebook ads for local business: we scored 355 US advertisers on four basics, from the ad to the page](https://mediapuppies.com/blog/facebook-ads-for-local-business/): Only 26.2% of the 355 US local advertisers we scored passed all four basics: an offer in the ad, a clear ask in the ad, a way to call or enquire on the first phone screen of the landing page, and Meta pixel code on that page. 2% passed none. The offer was the basic most often missing. 54.1% had an offer in at least one ad's text, against 66.8% with Meta pixel code on the page, 76.6% with a way to act on the first screen and 79.2% with a clear ask. Of the 163 advertisers with no offer in their ad text, 43 (26.4%) had a free offer such as a free consultation or estimate on the landing page. Advertisers whose ads had both an offer and a clear ask were more likely to have Meta pixel code on the page (74.9% against 59.6%), but no more likely to show a way to act on the first screen (74.3% against 78.7%). Med spas had the highest all-four rate, 33.1%. Real estate agents had the lowest, 14%, and 14% of them passed none of the four.
- [Landing page statistics 2026: we opened the pages behind 420 local advertisers' Facebook ads on a phone](https://mediapuppies.com/blog/landing-page-statistics/): Of the 363 pages that loaded, 39.1% were the advertiser's home page and 25.6% a separate landing page with no menu into a wider site. Home service firms used the home page most, at 55.8%. Of the 353 pages on advertisers' own sites, 112 (31.7%) loaded no Meta pixel during our visit: 47.2% of home pages against 12.9% of separate landing pages. 74.4% of pages had a tap-to-call link, but only 55.1% showed one on the first screen of a phone. Law firms led at 78.9%; med spas were at 35.3%. 120 pages (33.1%) had a form asking for contact details. Where nothing covered the screen, only 17 of 107 forms (15.9%) were on the first screen. The median form asked 5 questions. The median page transferred 2.5 MB, close to the 2.56 MB median for mobile home pages across the web. 17.1% were over 5 MB. 13 of the 420 advertisers' links (3.1%) were broken: dead domains, error pages, unusable certificates or a parked domain.
- [What is a good CTR in 2026? Click-through rates by platform and industry, with real results from YouTube](https://mediapuppies.com/blog/good-ctr/): CTR (click-through rate) is clicks divided by impressions, times 100. What counts as good depends almost entirely on where the ad runs. WordStream's 2026 data on 13,474 US search campaigns puts the median Google search CTR at 6.64%, from 5.56% for auto repair to 12.75% for arts and entertainment. Facebook traffic campaigns had a median CTR of 1.93% and lead campaigns 2.70%, across 1,829 US campaigns. Display ads ran at 0.12% to 0.40% by industry, so a search ad gets roughly 17 to 55 times the clicks per impression of a display ad, depending on the industry. Six video creators named 1% as the line for a workable or good CTR, and a seventh said his agency usually sees 1% to 2% on Meta. The real tests we found on ChatGPT and Reddit landed between 0.83% and 1.01%. Meta reports more than one CTR. The two most used are CTR (all), which counts every click on the ad, and link CTR, which counts only clicks to your site; one media buyer's benchmarks are 2% and 1%.
- [What do real estate leads cost in 2026? Zillow's new fee, and the Facebook, Google and ChatGPT numbers agents showed on YouTube](https://mediapuppies.com/blog/real-estate-leads-cost/): Zillow is moving its buyer leads to Zillow Preferred, where agents pay nothing upfront and hand over 15% to 40% of their commission at closing. Two-thirds of buyer connections went to Preferred agents in Q3 2026, and Zillow expects 100% in the first half of 2027. An Orange County agent who spent about nine months on Zillow Flex says Flex agents pay Zillow 40% at closing, and agents on his team kept 25% of the commission. A Maryland agent got 10 deals from Zillow; one neighbourhood cost him almost $1,600 a month, where a closing may pay $13,000 or more. The real Facebook lead costs shown ran from $4 to $10. One Texas campaign spent $2,184 for 283 leads at $7.72 each, and its first closing, worth $10,710 in commission, came in month five. A Toronto team leader paid an agency while his cost per lead climbed to about $80. His own campaigns now get leads at $4 to $6. An Austin agent spent $1,300 on ChatGPT ads for 13 seller leads, about $100 each, at a $63 cost per 1,000 impressions. We screened 69 videos: 36 were more than a year old, and only 14 of the 30 recent ones gave a number we could use. 50% of the 104 numbers came from a real account.
- [What is CPM, and what does it cost in 2026? Real numbers from Meta, Google, Reddit and ChatGPT ads](https://mediapuppies.com/blog/what-is-cpm/): CPM is the price of 1,000 ad impressions: spend divided by impressions, times 1,000. It is also CPC times CTR times 1,000, which is how you can estimate it when a platform does not report it. Two Meta ad accounts shown on screen in 2026 had CPMs of $10 to $30: a supplement brand at $30 in the US alone and $10 for the US plus other markets, and a new toy brand at $25 in December. The same creator says brand-new US supplement brands can see $145 to $200. ChatGPT ads were reported at about $60 per 1,000 impressions at launch. The three real accounts in our videos paid CA$26 to CA$34, $63, and about $120. Display was the cheapest: one advertiser's Google awareness campaigns came to about $5.79 per 1,000 impressions over their lifetime, and WordStream's 2026 display medians, across Google, YouTube, Meta and other networks, imply roughly $5.85 to $8.38 in six industries. A Reddit test that spent $80 bought 9,244 impressions, about $8.65 per 1,000. Only 7 of the 30 CPM numbers in these videos came from a real account. The rest were rules of thumb, worked examples, reported prices and two unsourced averages.
- [What do Angi leads cost in 2026? 214 numbers from 25 YouTube videos on Angi, Thumbtack and Google LSA](https://mediapuppies.com/blog/angi-leads-cost/): We screened 70 YouTube videos and kept 25 uploaded between 5 November 2025 and 28 October 2026 that state concrete lead numbers for Angi, Thumbtack or Google Local Services Ads: 214 numbers, 183 of them about these platforms or lead marketplaces in general. Only two videos showed real Angi spend. An HVAC company in Ontario paid $80 a lead (the video does not say which dollars) for 60 leads and closed 3 jobs, $1,600 per job. An electrician in Louisiana turned one $24 lead into about $66,000 of work. On Angi's May 2026 earnings call, CEO Jeff Kip said pros pay $50 a lead, win 1 in 7 or 1 in 8, and the average job is about $4,000. Angi's Q1 2026 release reported 105,000 average monthly active US pros, down 22% in a year. Videos claimed a marketplace lead goes to as many as 10 other contractors. Angi's own help pages cap each request at five pros, and Thumbtack limits a customer to five pros in the first four hours. On a podcast about Google Local Services Ads, Sam Preston of the agency Service Scalers read out cost per lead a year apart: roofing $74 to $107, electrical $29 to $43, plumbing $70 to $66. He did not say whether these were LSA only. Only 24.8% of the numbers came from a real account, and 27.6% were worked examples. For Thumbtack it was 1 of 21, and 7 more were prices on one owner's screen.
- [AI Overviews on the searches advertisers pay for: 339 US Google Ads keywords, 118 of them also checked in the UK, Canada and Australia](https://mediapuppies.com/blog/ai-overviews-ads-study/): On 3 November 2026 Google showed an AI Overview on 196 of 339 US searches that advertisers pay for (57.8%). Leaving out "near me" searches, it was 175 of 278 (62.9%). Cost questions almost always got one: 33 of 36 (91.7%), and all 33 of those AI Overviews quoted dollar figures. The priciest clicks were not spared. With near-me searches left out, keywords with an estimated CPC of $30 or more showed an AI Overview 62.5% of the time, against 63.1% below $30. Cheaper keywords got more overall, mostly because cheap cost questions almost always get one. With near-me searches left out, every insurance and software keyword showed an AI Overview. Home service searches other than cost questions showed one only 39.1% of the time, and legal searches 44.8%. At least 128 of the 196 US AI Overviews (65.3%) asked the searcher a question, such as their city, budget or loan amount. Among the 135 we captured in full, 128 did (94.8%). On 95 searches run in all four countries the rates were close: Australia 80%, Canada 74.7%, the UK 73.7% and the US 72.6%. With a single run, that order could easily change.
- [How much do Facebook ads cost in 2026? 212 numbers from 29 YouTube videos by ad buyers and marketers](https://mediapuppies.com/blog/facebook-ads-cost/): We screened 69 YouTube videos and kept 29 uploaded between November 2025 and November 2026 that state concrete Facebook ad costs, 212 numbers in all. Where a country was named it was the US, UK or Australia. Eight videos reported a real cost per lead. Four fell between $7.72 and $21.80, and the range ran from $1 to $2 for a free B2B guide to a roofing campaign that started at $25 and rose past $50. None of the 9 CPM figures came from a real ad account, and 7 were worked examples. The only cited average was $8.15. WordStream and LocalIQ's 2026 report on 452 US lead campaigns put the median cost per lead at $27.39, with real estate at $13.74 and home improvement at $42.95. Seven channels named a starting budget, from $10 to $100 a day, with a median of $35. In case-study videos 79.3% of the numbers came from a real account. In cost, budget and how-to videos it was 20%, and 37.5% were worked examples.
- [Dental marketing in 2026: what patient clicks cost on Google, and what 99 advertisers run on Facebook](https://mediapuppies.com/blog/dental-marketing-data/): Across 37 US patient keywords, the median Google cost per click was $6.39. Implants and dentures had the highest group median at $10.26, driven by implants. For treatment searches, adding "near me" raised the click price sharply: by 82% for dental implants and 130% for Invisalign. For general searches such as "dentist" it barely moved. Price searches were cheaper than the treatment itself in all 5 pairs with an estimate, for example $3.23 for "invisalign cost" against $4.68 for "invisalign". One implant chain ran 73 of the 192 live dental ads on Facebook and Instagram. Across the other 98 advertisers' 119 ads, single images led at 42% and video was 26.9%. 71.4% of those 119 ads had been running for a year or more, and the median ad had been live for 456 days.
- [Facebook Ad Library study: what 673 live US ads from law firms, dentists, real estate and home services show](https://mediapuppies.com/blog/facebook-ad-library-study/): On 3 November 2026 the median active ad had already been live for 271 days, and 42.6% of the 673 ads had been running for a year or more. 79.6% of the 427 advertisers had exactly one active ad. In real estate the figure was 92%. Formats split by trade: 37% of law firm ads were video, against 11.1% for home services, where 52.1% were single images. 28.7% of law firm ads offered something free, usually a consultation, and 21.4% of home service ads offered a free estimate or inspection. Of 99 real estate ads aimed at buyers, sellers or renters, 88.9% carried Meta's Housing label. 11 did not.
- [How much does Google Ads cost for home services? We priced 169 keywords in 8 trades.](https://mediapuppies.com/blog/google-ads-cost-home-services/): Across 169 US home service keywords, the median Google Ads cost per click was $17.62, and the middle half ran from $7.73 to $25.63. Water damage had the priciest clicks (median $33.84) and locksmith the cheapest ($5.80). The most expensive single keyword was emergency water damage restoration at $66.23. Emergency searches had a median CPC of $27.91: 1.36 times repair searches and 4.49 times price-research searches. Adding "near me" made no consistent difference. It raised the CPC in 9 of 17 keyword pairs, by a median of $0.21. Install and replacement keywords cost a median $13.05 a click, against $20.45 for repair keywords.
- [Law firm marketing in 2026: what Google clicks cost by practice area, and what 146 firms run on Facebook](https://mediapuppies.com/blog/law-firm-marketing-data/): Personal injury keywords had a median US Google cost per click of $156, 16.08 times the median for the other practice areas we checked ($9.70). The priciest keyword we checked was truck accident lawyer, at an estimated $252.78 a click. All eight of the most expensive keywords were injury searches. The "near me" version had a lower CPC estimate in 4 of the 5 legal keyword pairs we compared. On Facebook and Instagram, the median live law firm ad had been running for 181 days, and 28.7% offered something free, such as a consultation or case review. 10.6% of law firm ads were in Spanish or bilingual, and 22 of those 28 were immigration ads.
- [We analysed 439 live US med spa ads in the Meta Ad Library. Here is what they run.](https://mediapuppies.com/blog/med-spa-meta-ads-study/): 80.1% of the 296 med spa advertisers we found had exactly one active ad. Only 2.7% were running five or more. The median med spa ad had been live for 160 days, and 69% had been running for 90 days or longer. 60.1% of ads mentioned a price or a discount, and 28.7% were built around a new-client special. Book now was the most common button, on 32.6% of ads. 53.3% sent people to the clinic's own website. Of 180 ads for Botox-type treatments, 83.9% named a brand such as Botox or Dysport in the copy.
- [Real estate marketing in 2026: the median seller click costs 16 times a buyer click, and what 87 advertisers run on Facebook](https://mediapuppies.com/blog/real-estate-marketing-data/): Our six seller searches had a median US Google cost per click of $25.41, about 16 times the $1.61 median for six buyer searches. Sell-now searches drove it; value checks cost under $3. "Sell my house" was estimated at $69.29 a click and "we buy houses" $40.68, while "homes for sale" was $0.48. Searches for an agent cost from $7.30 ("realtor near me") to $13.21 ("listing agent"); the five in our agents group had a median of $8. In our Facebook Ad Library sample, 92% of the 87 real estate advertisers appeared with just one ad, and the median ad had been running for 347 days. 88.9% of the 99 consumer real estate ads carried Meta's Housing label, and 19.2% were catalog ads built from a listing feed.
- [What is CPC? Cost per click explained, with Google Ads CPC estimates for 339 US keywords across 11 industries](https://mediapuppies.com/blog/what-is-cpc/): Across 339 US keywords in 11 industries, the median estimated Google Ads cost per click was $12.32, pulled up by 169 home service keywords. The median of the 11 industry medians was $9.47. Among our samples, insurance had the highest industry median at $35.44 (4 of its 10 keywords were quote searches) and ecommerce the lowest at $2.08, about 17 times lower. 12 keywords cost $100 or more per click: 11 personal injury searches and google ads management at $228.10. Insurance searches asking for a quote had a median of $71.04 across 4 keywords, against $19.14 for 6 other insurance searches. The four cheapest clicks were home-buying and rental searches: condos for sale was estimated at $0.34 a click.

- [Paying an Indian agency from overseas: invoices, FX and tax](https://mediapuppies.com/blog/paying-an-indian-agency/): The mechanics of paying an Indian agency from abroad: invoicing currency, GST on exported services, transfer routes, and who absorbs the bank fees.
- [Planning for Q4 in the US: what actually happens to costs](https://mediapuppies.com/blog/us-q4-ad-costs-planning/): Q4 ad costs in the US climb from October, peak around Black Friday and Cyber Monday, and fall in January. How to budget for it rather than react.
- [Why your US conversions fell and nobody changed anything](https://mediapuppies.com/blog/us-state-privacy-consent-conversions/): US state privacy laws, Global Privacy Control and consent mode quietly cut the conversion data reaching Meta and Google. How to tell if it is you.
- [Lead forms that will actually be followed up: US consent wording](https://mediapuppies.com/blog/us-lead-form-consent-language/): If your US leads will be called or texted, the lead form consent wording next to the submit button matters. What belongs on it, and who writes it.
- [Special Ad Categories: why your US targeting disappeared](https://mediapuppies.com/blog/meta-special-ad-categories-us/): Housing, employment, credit and social issues strip most Meta targeting in the US. What special ad categories remove, what stays, and how to adapt.
- [Local Services Ads: the US listing above your search ads](https://mediapuppies.com/blog/google-local-services-ads-us/): How Google Local Services Ads work for US home service firms in 2026: lead costs by trade, the move into Google Ads, missed-call charges and verification.
- [PECR, consent mode, and the UK conversions you stopped seeing](https://mediapuppies.com/blog/uk-consent-mode-conversion-loss/): UK cookie consent is governed by PECR, and how consent mode is wired decides how much data reaches Meta and Google. How to diagnose a sudden drop.
- [The UK retail calendar: planning around Black Friday and Boxing Day](https://mediapuppies.com/blog/uk-retail-seasonality-planning/): UK retail seasonality has two peaks rather than one, and January behaves differently here than elsewhere. How to budget for the real shape of the year.
- [Financial promotions in the UK: the rule that stops campaigns dead](https://mediapuppies.com/blog/fca-financial-promotions-paid-media/): Promoting an investment, credit product or crypto to UK consumers means the financial promotions rules apply. What that does to a paid media plan.
- [Advertising in Canada: what Indian export brands should know](https://mediapuppies.com/blog/advertising-in-canada/): Advertising in Canada looks like the US and is not. Bilingual requirements, anti-spam law, provincial privacy rules and a thinner auction all change the plan.
- [Why 30 June is Australia’s biggest month and your calendar missed it](https://mediapuppies.com/blog/australia-eofy-marketing/): EOFY marketing in Australia: why the run-up to 30 June is a real demand spike for anything a business can expense, and how to plan ads around it.

## Marketing economics
